newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids hold despite softer crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids hold despite softer crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady again Friday in sluggish trade, with some utility demand in Florida offsetting softer crude and physical gas prices, industry sources said.

"No one's panicking because crude is down. Resid is not going to react immediately to weaker crude. The competition is gas," said one cash trader, noting there was decent demand in Florida despite the mild East Coast weather this week that has undermined utility burns in the Northeast.
But a surge in East Coast city gate gas prices this week gave resid a competitive edge, setting the stage for better fuel oil demand if warmer temperatures return.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were steady to up again, with three percent gaining slightly to $15.25, while one percent was flat at about $16, traders said.
In New York Harbor, most grades were stable, with 0.3 percent high pour still well supported in the low-$18s by an 850,000 barrel August HP buy program for one New York utility.
NYH physical one percent was unchanged at about $16, but September one percent paper slipped 10-15 cents to the $16.15-30 area with softer crude.
High sulphurs in New York mostly held steady, with 2.2 percent still talked on either side of $15.00, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were confirmed.

New York city gate weekend gas prices slumped about a dime Friday to the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $15.94 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was down a similar amount to the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or about $15.06 a barrel.
